Q1: Should this fix also cover the three `orchestrate-poll` failures in `tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py`, which have nothing to do with the new label?
Choices:
A) No. Fix only the two certain failures: add `"ai:waiting-on-dependency"` right after `"ai:blocked"` in `PHASE_LABELS`, and add `"blocker_runs": [], "blocker_paths": []` to the test's `args`. Leave the untrusted-input contract failures to a separate issue or a later triage generation, accepting that `orchestrate-poll` stays red on PR #8883 until then.
B) Yes. Make all three CI worker jobs green on the PR branch. Do the two certain fixes, then fix each of the three untrusted-input contract failures where it starts. If the workflow or script is correct and the test setup is missing something (for example `RUN_PLAN_CODEX_SUPPORT_DIR` not set in `_run_evidence_block`), fix the test. If a `for f in gh_helpers.sh ...; do` staging loop in `clarify.yml`/`implement.yml` lost `attempt_journal.py`/`evidence_pack.py`, restore the staged file in the workflow. Never weaken an assertion. Leave the `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` failure alone, since it's an external limit. (RECOMMENDED)
C) Partly. Do the two certain fixes plus only the failures PR #8883's own diff caused, as shown by comparing the PR head with the default branch. Leave failures that already exist on the default branch for a separate issue.
